Rarity.rationale: Matches FestivePopper.cs:15, and it is what makes the relic obtainable: executed (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b05.py b05-pool) festive_popper is in the transcribed grab bag at Common rarity.

AfterPlayerTurnStart.issue: Rollup of guards G1, G2 and G3 per binding rule 4. The effect's numbers are right -- DamageVar(9m, ValueProp.Unpowered) (FestivePopper.cs:17) vs DAMAGE = 9 at DamageProps.NON_CARD_UNPOWERED (festive_popper.py:19, :27), no AscensionHelper branch in the file, dealer = the player on both sides, turn 1 only -- but the hook slot is a step late (G1), the enemy set is built from a weaker predicate (G2), and the win check the source performs after the whole turn-start sequence is hand-rolled inline instead (G3).

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): C#'s hook is AfterPlayerTurnStart, turn_structure step 22; the sim's on_player_turn_started is the step-23 AfterSideTurnStart slot
guards.issue: MECHANISM: step 22 is `await CardPileCmd.Draw(...)` then `await Hook.AfterPlayerTurnStart(state, choiceContext, player)` (CombatManager.cs:673-675), which itself runs Early -> plain -> Late passes (Hook.cs:882-908); step 23 is Hook.AfterSideTurnStart (CombatManager.cs:520-524). The sim has one post-draw slot for both and dispatches it in registration order -- relics/base.py:15-17's mapping table says as much, and the executed order (py audit/tools/relic_probes.py turn-order) confirms on_player_turn_started is that single slot. Same collapse as relic/bag_of_marbles G1 and relic/fake_blood_vial G2 in this batch; PROMPT.md bug class 11. DORMANT: nothing runs between the two C# steps in single-player, so the only observable is the relative order of a step-22 and a step-23 listener. The one that matters is C#'s auto-pre-play phase, step 26, which is strictly AFTER both -- so in C# the Popper's 9 damage always precedes a turn-1 auto-play, while in the sim the Imbued enchantment's auto-play fires from the SAME on_player_turn_started dispatch and cards are registered before relics (combat.py:124-133 then :158-159), so the auto-play goes FIRST. That is audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json gap G2 (cards-before-relics) and audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json gap G8 (the auto-pre-play phase's position); one verdict per mechanism, binding rule 3, and dormant here because no ported auto-play's outcome depends on 9 damage having landed. Porting an auto-played card that reads enemy HP or count makes it live. Rule 7: CombatManager.cs, Hook.cs, relics/base.py and combat.py are unhashed here.

Identical mechanism to relic/bag_of_marbles guard G2 and carried with the same gap verdict per binding rule 3, at another turn-1 all-enemies effect. C# targets `Enemies.Where(e => e.IsHittable)` (CombatState.cs:142) and IsHittable is `!IsDead && Hook.ShouldAllowHitting(CombatState, this)` (Creature.cs:285-299); Relic.living_enemies filters on `not e.is_gone` ONLY (relics/base.py:294-297), and its own docstring concedes the should_allow_hitting predicate is left to DamageCmd. DORMANT, with the dormancy argument re-executed for this relic rather than inherited: py audit/tools/relic_probes_b05.py popper-win prints the living_enemies list and confirms hooks.should_allow_hitting exists but is not consulted by living_enemies; bag_of_marbles' record establishes that the only ported should_allow_hitting implementer gates on IllusionPower's mid-revival state, which cannot be true during turn 1 -- the only turn either relic fires. There is a partial backstop here that Bag of Marbles lacks: DamageCmd.deal itself calls hooks.should_allow_hitting and returns 0 (cmds.py:49-50), so an unhittable enemy would take no damage even though the sim iterated over it -- the residual divergence is the on_attacked/history entry and any per-target side effect, not the HP. Porting a turn-1 untargetable enemy makes it live. Rule 7: CombatState.cs, Creature.cs, relics/base.py and cmds.py are unhashed here.

guards.what: G3 (DORMANT): the port hand-rolls `self._check_win()` (festive_popper.py:28) where C# reaches CheckWinCondition only after the whole turn-start sequence
guards.issue: MECHANISM: C# runs CheckWinCondition at CombatManager.cs:573 -- step 27, AFTER step 23's AfterSideTurnStart pass, step 24's orb tick and step 26's auto-pre-play phase. Relic._check_win (relics/base.py:299-303) ends the combat the instant the last enemy dies, in the middle of the on_player_turn_started dispatch. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b05.py popper-win): with a lethal turn-1 Popper, a listener registered AFTER the relic and reached later in the same dispatch observes is_over=True, phase=COMBAT_OVER and enemy_hp=[0], where C# is still mid-step-23 with the combat live. This is audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json gap G13, which labels the mechanism LIVE and cites festive_popper.py:21 by name as one of the seven turn-start listeners that deal damage, noting that the relic's hand-rolled _check_win exists 'precisely because this check is missing' -- one verdict per mechanism, binding rule 3, so this entry does not re-derive it; the seam owns the missing check and this record owns the relic's observable. DORMANT AT THIS SITE, in the direction that matters: the compensating call means the Popper does NOT leave a won combat running (the failure G13 pins with an xfail is player death, which this relic cannot cause -- it damages enemies only). What remains is the early end, which suppresses any later same-dispatch listener that C# would still run. Porting a turn-1 listener whose effect matters after the last enemy dies -- a reward-side or on-victory counter -- makes it live. Rule 7: CombatManager.cs and relics/base.py are unhashed here.

guards.what: N1: C# damages every enemy in ONE multi-target CreatureCmd.Damage call (FestivePopper.cs:28); the sim loops per enemy (festive_popper.py:24-28)
guards.rationale: Same treatment and same verdict as relic/bag_of_marbles' N2 (binding rule 3): both iterate the enemy list in index order with the same amount, props and dealer, and the sim's loop merely makes the order explicit. audit/records/seam/damage_pipeline.json's spec confirms CreatureCmd.Damage is a per-target loop internally, with a `dealer.IsDead` bail before the loop and an `originalTarget.IsDead` skip inside it -- the sim's living_enemies pre-filter plus DamageCmd.deal's own guards cover the same ground for a turn-1 effect where the dealer is the just-alive player. The enemy SET is G2's subject, not this entry's. Rule 7: damage_pipeline's sources are unhashed here.

The owner check is structurally satisfied -- the sim dispatches on_player_turn_started once, for the one player (player.py:186) -- and `self.turn == 1` (festive_popper.py:22) is the same comparison against the same 1-based counter (executed turn-order probe prints turn=1 for the first player turn). Note C# uses `== 1` here where its sibling FakeBloodVial.cs:21 uses `<= 1`; the sim mirrors each relic's own operator. Rule 7: player.py and FakeBloodVial.cs are unhashed here.
